full_judgment:
7. The learned Counsel for the respondent No. 1 submitted that the trial Curt, discussing in details the evidence on record, many of which were admitted ones, and also answering all the points raised by both the parties, gave a part decree for Taka 33,45,276.24 against claim of the respondent No, 1 for Taka 66,06,500 on disallowing many claims of the respondent No.1 and at the same time allowing some of the claims of the port authority against the respondent No. 1 and the High Court Division, having gone through the evidence and the materials on record also found that in respect of many of the documentary evidence there were no dispute and then on discussing the evidence of both the sides, though in brief, found that the judgment of the trial Court contained all the points raised by the parties and findings of the trial Court are based on material evidence on record; during hearing before the High Court Division the learned Advocate for the appellant could not point out any misreading or non-consideration of the evidence on record and/or any illegality or infirmity in the findings of the trial court; the judgment of the High Court Division being a judgment of affirmance there was also no requirement of the High Court Division to discuss in detail the evidence adduced by the patties. The learned Counsel also submitted that the trial Court found that the port authority by not supplying the raw materials as per terms of the contract tailed to perform their part under the contract and the respondent No.1, on being assured by the port authority that they after obtaining permission from the Ministry would pay the running bills covering the excess amount for purchasing the materials from outside, procured the materials from market at a higher rate and completed the works to some extent on the basis of the above assurance but ultimately, the port authority did not make payment against the bills for the excess amount and in that situation the respondent No. 1 had no other alternative but to stop the remaining works and the High Court Division having dismissed the appeal affirming the concurrent findings of facts as above the decision of the High Court Division does not call for any interference. 

 10. At the end of the above paragraph 21 the port authority further stated that a sum of Taka 18,85,000 only is due to the respondent No. 1 from the port authority against security deposit of Taka 18,57,126 and Taka 21,640 which the respondent No.1 would get against Group B work and that after adjustment of the above amount of Taka 18,85,000 from the claim of the port authority against materials which stood at Taka 10,85,000 against 25,000 sft of boulders, advance mobilisation bill, rent of roller, bills against water and electricity, the respondent No. 1 is entitled to claim from the port authority only a sum of Taka 6,55,463 and further since the port authority had to spend a sum of Taka 15,23,899 for completing the above works by re- tender the above amount is also due from the respondent No.1 

 25. The learned trial judge accordingly held that the contracts between the respondent No. 1 and the port authority are enforceable and that at the late stage the defendants deviating from the terms of the contract stopped supplying materials and since the materials were to be supplied by the port authority there was no requirement for the respondent No. 1 to purchase the materials from the open market at higher rate and that is why the respondent No.1, for above works, quoted 9% below the estimated costs and otherwise the respondent No.1 in their offers would have quoted 9 to 10% above the estimated costs. The learned trial judge then after calculating the claims found that though the respondent No.1 claimed Taka 20,00,000 against the security deposit, in fact a sum of Taka 18,35,487 is due to him against security and the dues against construction of Group B works stood at Taka 21,640; the dues against purchase of 271.63 of MS rod against four groups of Open Stock Yard and 52.4 tons of MS rod against Overhead Tank with additional amount of Taka 4500 per ton stood at Taka 12,12,335 and Taka 2,35,850 respectively, total being Taka 14,58,135; the dues against 7525 bags of cement in respect offour groups of Open Stock Yard and 1825 bags of cement in respect of Overhead Tank with additional amount of Taka 35 per bag stood at Taka 2,63,375 and Taka 73,875 respectively, total being Taka 3,27,250; the dues against the salaries of the staff deployed in the above two works stood at Taka 3,80,000; the dues against 2 mixture machines rented for Open Stock Yard and Overhead Tank stood at Taka 1,80,000 and thus total dues of the respondent No.1 stood at Taka 42,02,511. The learned trial judge also found that though the port authority claimed a sum of Taka 10,85,000 against excess payment, against bills of boulders, mobilization bill, rent of roller, electricity and water bills in respect of Groups A, C and D, but the actual dues is Taka 8,57,234.86 and accordingly, on deducting the above amount of Taka 8,57,234.86 from the above amount of Taka 42,02,511, passed a decree for Taka 33,45,276.14, i.e. the balance amount. 

 "We have gone through the evidence, both oral and documentary. Some of the documentary evidence are admitted and that there was no dispute over them.' We have also gone through the judgment of the trial Court. It is an elaborate description as well as a big judgment containing all the points raised by the parties. Not only that, the learned Judge has discussed each and every aspect of the case and with much pain he has calculated the claims of the plaintiff and the defendants. He has discussed the evidence in such a manner which do not require any repetition by this Court. The discussions and findings were based on material evidence on record and the learned Advocate for the appellant in fact failed to point out any material irregularities or flaws or illegality in the findings of the trial Court. After discussing the material evidence on record in details the learned Subordinate Judge has come to a finding that dues of the plaintiff from the defendants stood at Taka 42,02,511. He has shown the dues of the plaintiff item by item from serial Nos. 1 to 5 and calculating the different amounts the learned judge found that dues of the plaintiff from the defendants stood at the above amount. The leaned Judge also calculated the dues of the defendants from the plaintiff item wise from item Nos. 1 to 4 and found that the dues of the defendants from plaintiff stood at Taka 8,57,234.86. So, after deducting the aforesaid dues of the defendants the aforesaid dues of the defendant from the plaintiff not dues stood at Taka 33,45,276.14 and for that amount the learned Sub-Judge passed a decree in favour of the plaintiff with interest as stated in the judgment." 

 28. Now regarding the submission of the learned Counsel of the appellant as stated earlier to the effect that the respondent No. 1 failed to complete the construction work within the stipulated time and the High Court Division did not decide the effect of such breach, from the depositions of witnesses as quoted above, it will appear that regarding delay PW 1 in his examination in-chief stated that in view of the failure of the port authority to supply the materials, the construction works were about to be stopped and at that time the port authority requested the respondent No.1 to continue with the works by purchasing the materials from outside at market price assuring that the excess amount, if any, to be spent by the respondent No.1 over the schedule rate will be paid by the port authority and accordingly, the respondent No. 1 went on with the construction works by purchasing materials from the market at the prevailing rate, which was higher than the schedule rate, and then when he used to ask the port authority for payment of the bills in respect of the excess amount they used to assure him that after approval of the Ministry the same will be paid but the port authority did not pay the excess amount which the respondent No. 1 had to spend for purchasing the MS rods and cement and other materials from the market at higher rate and so the construction works, which in the meantime were going on slowly, were stopped; for the stoppage of the construction works the port authority is responsible and if they would have supplied' the materials as per terms of the contract the respondent No.1 could complete the works within the time; PW 1 voluntarily stated that আমাকে যখন যতটুকু মাল সরবরাহ করা হইয়াছে তখন সেই ভাবে ততটুকু কাজ আমি করিয়াছি।”,  DW 1, in his cross-examination, admitted that the time prescribed for completion of the work as mentioned against different items of the contract may be changed considering the position of the works and other circumstances and the port authority may extend the time if found reasonable; in the month of December 1988 due to excessive increase of the price of materials the construction works were closed; the port authority extended the time in respect of works of some of the items; if the port authority could supply the materials in due time the respondent No.1 could finish the incomplete works within time.
